subject.title: Telegram should default to allowlist mode with owner ID

question: Should fresh Telegram onboarding establish the owner through a one-time verification challenge and immediately persist allowlist state, or bootstrap through pairing and transition only after explicit owner approval?
rationale: Both designs address unsolicited pairing exposure, but they define different initial trust, failure recovery, and alignment with the cross-channel post-bootstrap proposal; repository evidence cannot choose that contract safely.

options.title: Challenge-verified onboarding
options.body: Require the intended owner to return a one-time token, then atomically persist the numeric sender ID and allowlist policy.

options.title: Post-pairing transition
options.body: Keep pairing for first access and explicitly convert the approved owner into allowlist state afterward, coordinating with the cross-channel proposal.

options.title: Retain pairing default
options.body: Leave authorization behavior unchanged and improve warnings plus manual numeric-ID setup only.

recommendation.title: Challenge-verified onboarding
recommendation.body: Require the intended owner to return a one-time token, then atomically persist the numeric sender ID and allowlist policy.

likelyOwner.reason: He has the strongest history signal across the Telegram setup surface and its major boundary refactors.
